A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the covariant three-dimensional equations are a gauge-invariant approximation to the corresponding four-dimensional equations, which is a generalization of the nonrelativistic three-dimensional equations.
a covariant gauge-invariant three-dimensional description of relativistic bound states has been developed.

we have developed a covariant three-dimensional gauge-invariant formalism that allows the construction of a gauge-invariant amplitude for a bound state interacting with an external electromagnetic field, and we have applied this formalism to the construction of a three-dimensional bound-state equation for the deuteron.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gauge-invariant three-dimensional bound state equations are obtained from four-dimensional ones in the same manner as the three-dimensional scattering equations.
the three-dimensional equations for bound states are not only covariant, but also gauge-invariant.
the gauge-invariant formalism is not restricted to a single coupling-constant order.
